headline: Biological priors and cross-modal alignment shape histology and single-cell embeddings
label: Biomolecular Representation Learning
summary: Recent preprints extend representation learning for pathology, spatial transcriptomics, and cytometry with explicit biological structure built into their…
synthesis: The common thread is that representation and generative models for histology, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell data are being constrained by explicit biological structure rather than trained on raw features alone. Program-space Diffusion predicts cNMF-derived transcriptional programs instead of individual genes, and PaSTel pretrains hierarchically with biological priors and contrastive alignment between histology images and gene expression. Disentangled latents recur across the set: shared versus private latents for paired H&E and spatial transcriptomics, cell-type, batch and residual latents in scDIVA, and separation of technical batch effects from biological signal in Kanade. Discrete cell and niche codes in SQUINT and inspectable gating in scDNM-VAE target interpretability. What is new is structure written into the objective or architecture itself. The set is heterogeneous, however: pathology MIL methods such as KHiM-Mamba and SLMP and the open-weight cytometry foundation model CytoBERT address adjacent problems.
